description: Work inside web pages in the paired Chrome profile with the user's existing logins: read page text and controls (including content inside cross-origin iframes, such as embedded third-party widgets), click, type, fill forms, select options, check boxes, hover, navigate, go back/forward, reload, press keys, scroll, wait for elements, URLs, load states, or text, capture screenshots, search history, use the clipboard, upload files, wait for downloads, read console logs, export pages as MHTML, and list or invoke native page WebMCP tools when present. Prefer this tool over computer for anything inside a web page. This choice is between the computer and browser tools only; it does not forbid another browser route the user explicitly authorizes, such as Playwright connectOverCDP to an existing Chrome DevTools endpoint, which stays subject to the same permission, guardrail, credential and confirmation rules. Observations return readable text plus semantic elements, and an element's optional frame field names the iframe page it came from (frames lists child frames and whether each was observed). Use status once, then tabs. Reuse returned tabID, generation, documentGeneration, and observationRevision fences exactly as numbers; never invent refs. Observe for semantic refs, then act only by a returned ref; each element also carries a stable locator (role and accessible name), and click, type, fill, select, check, hover, upload, and wait accept that locator instead of a ref when the same element must be found again after re-observing; wait also accepts a locator for an element that has not appeared yet. Observe with diff:true to receive only elements added or changed since the previous observation, with removed locators listed in delta; the first observation is always full. Action results return updated tab fences, not a semantic observation; carry those fences forward for actions without refs, and observe again before another ref-based action because each action invalidates prior refs. Capture only when semantic observation is insufficient; capture accepts a clip rectangle, fullPage:true for the whole page, or a ref to capture one element. Fill replaces a field's text (text:'' clears it); select picks options of a native select by values, labels, or indexes, or one option of an open listbox by label or index; check sets a checkbox, radio, or switch to checked:true or checked:false and does nothing when it already matches; hover moves the pointer over an element without clicking. These return the control's resulting state. Upload takes absolute file paths and a file input, including one listed as a hidden file input, or the element that opens a file chooser; no native file dialog opens, and a page picker without a file input cannot receive files; isolated mode rejects upload. Elements report checked, pressed, expanded, selected, and the value of ordinary fields; sensitive:true marks a password, one-time-code, or payment field whose value is withheld and which no action may fill. Wait takes one condition: a ref or locator with state attached, visible, hidden, or detached (default visible for a locator, attached for a ref); url, a pattern over the page origin and path where * matches any characters; load: domcontentloaded, load, or networkidle (no network request pending for 500 ms; on a paired tab attached while requests were already running, only requests started after attach are seen); or text that must appear on the page. timeoutMs is at most 30,000; wait without a condition waits for load. key checks the active focus in profile, owned, and isolated modes. Only Tab, Shift+Tab, Escape, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home, End, PageUp, and PageDown bypass active-focus inspection, with no Ctrl, Meta, or Alt and Shift allowed only for Tab. Every other supported key requires verified focus, including printable characters with Shift or Alt, Space, Enter, Backspace, Delete, Insert, Shift+Insert, and all Ctrl or Meta chords, including V and X. Focus inspection refuses sensitive password, one-time-code, payment, or secret-named fields, file inputs, and unverified focus (including closed shadow roots and unreachable cross-origin frames) before any key event with dispatched:false. Do not use key to bypass a sensitive-field refusal in any mode. If a page opens a JavaScript dialog, other actions stall until it is answered: use action {type:'dialog'} to read it and {type:'dialog', accept:true or false, text} to respond. Mark an owned tab that holds the work product with operation:'deliver' so it stays open in Chrome for the user instead of closing when control ends. Ask the user before irreversible submissions, purchases, payments, deletions, sending messages, or accepting legal terms; proceed without asking for reading, navigation, and reversible input that does not submit anything. Never solve CAPTCHAs, enter passwords, one-time codes, or payment secrets: stop and hand the page to the user. On a stale-fence error, observe once and retry once; never replay an uncertain mutation—observe first. Prefer mode:'owned' background tabs for new work so user tabs stay untouched. Paired Chrome is the default; mode:'profile' selects it explicitly, and mode:'isolated' uses the user-started temporary headless browser. Profile tabs can group or ungroup granted inactive tabs. The first observe or action claims a profile tab for this Session; lease:'other' means another Session controls it, so choose another tab or wait. Call operation:'release' with mode:'profile' when finished with a tab; control also ends when the Session goes idle. Owned mode only creates and closes its own tabs. Focus emulation keeps controlled pages visible and unthrottled while attached; it ends when the debugger detaches.
